comparison: Both evaluations support the methodological and ethical procedures (C84-C86). OpenEval explicitly notes these are standard practices appropriately reported, while peer reviewers implicitly accepted them without raising concerns about experimental design or sample size.

Both strongly support the behavioral findings on distractor suppression (C25-C32). OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence with appropriate statistics and effect sizes, while peer reviewers explicitly acknowledged these results as supporting prior literature with no concerns raised.

Both support the dual-task memory findings (C23-C24). OpenEval notes statistical evidence for both disruption and maintained functional performance, while peer reviewers accepted the behavioral analyses examining memory-search relationships and alternative explanations due to dual-task design.

Both support the methodological innovation of the pinging technique (C71-C81). OpenEval describes it as a well-supported methodological contribution with demonstrated sensitivity, while peer reviewers praised it as creative and clever with 'a lot of potential value.'

Both address the core neural findings (C46-C51) but with different emphases. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to non-significant conditional difference (C48) and exploratory nature, while peer reviewers rated SUPPORTED, accepting these as the main contribution despite acknowledging openness to interpretation.

Both rate the main theoretical conclusion (reactive vs. proactive suppression) as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval cites non-significant comparisons, exploratory analyses, and unresolved alternative explanations. Peer reviewers similarly note results are 'open to multiple interpretations' and 'may still remain open to alternative explanations.'

Both support the cross-session IEM analysis and activity-silent memory findings (C40-C45). OpenEval notes support with caveat about debated ping mechanisms, while peer reviewers praised the methodological approach without raising concerns about these specific claims.

Both support the validation analyses (C35-C36). OpenEval emphasizes statistical evidence for no pre-existing bias and methodological foundation, while peer reviewers accepted these as part of the core neural contribution without specific concerns.

Both support the control analysis addressing alternative explanations (C65). OpenEval cites Figure 2 supplement data showing CTF modulations aren't due to memory performance changes, while peer reviewers acknowledged authors addressed alternative explanations satisfactorily.

Both support the intertrial control analysis (C33-C34). OpenEval explicitly notes this strengthens conclusions, while peer reviewers implicitly accepted it as part of methodological aspects that were 'largely addressed.'

OpenEval supports the literature review and theoretical framework (C1-C22), noting appropriate citations and well-documented characterization of the proactive vs. reactive debate. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addressed these background claims.

OpenEval supports the contextualization claims citing prior work on alpha power and behavioral findings (C58-C60, C64, C69-C70). No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addressed these literature contextualization claims.

OpenEval supports the acknowledgment of limitations and theoretical debates (C68, C74-C75, C78), viewing this as appropriate scientific caution. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted these caveats, with one noting the authors 'clarified and further discussed several methodological aspects, limitations, and alternative interpretations.'

Peer reviewers supported claim C4 (experimental design) and C52 (main conclusion about reactive suppression) as part of their evaluation. OpenEval addressed C52 in R6 (rated UNCERTAIN) but did not create a separate result for C4.

Peer reviewers addressed C7 (research question) and C22 (theoretical framework) as part of their UNCERTAIN evaluation of the main conclusion. OpenEval addressed C22 in R10 (literature review, rated SUPPORTED) but did not separately evaluate C7.
